## Hello World Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- LinkedIn uses machine learning (ML) to prioritize content smarter, not replace humans, but to help reviewers act faster, scale better, and keep the platform safe without losing judgment or nuance.
- The new ML-based review prioritization system scores content based on the probability of policy violation, pushing high-risk content to the top of the review queue.
- This approach has led to a ~10% of queued content being auto-decided, reduced load on human reviewers, ~60% faster detection of violations, and less harmful exposure for members.

### Detailed Points
- LinkedIn's Trust & Safety system combines automated AI models, member reports, and human reviewers to moderate content at scale.
- The old First-In-First-Out (FIFO) system was inefficient at scale, with most reviewed content being non-violating and harmful content potentially sitting in the queue for hours.
- The new system uses XGBoost models trained on historical moderation data to predict the likelihood of policy violation, with a focus on high precision and recall.
- The models are trained on a representative sample of past, human-labeled review data, evaluated on out-of-time datasets, and tuned using random grid search for hyperparameter optimization.
- The decision layer integrates with existing review assignment and prioritization tools, using ML-generated risk scores and static parameters to decide which items human reviewers should see first.
- The system has led to a significant reduction in harmful exposure for members, with ~60% faster detection of violations and ~10% of queued content being auto-decided.

## TAAFT - There's An AI For That

### Key Highlights
- A tiny island, Anguilla, has earned $70 million from AI domain registrations, which is nearly half of its government's budget.
- Apple's Siri is getting a Gemini upgrade, making it a full chatbot rival, with the ability to tap into personal data and on-screen content.
- Google has introduced a new way to train AI faster, called GIST, which provides mathematical guarantees that its selections hit at least 50% of optimal value.
- Rokid has launched AI Glasses that weigh 38.5 grams, support any prescription, and come with over 200 lens color options.

### Detailed Points
- Anguilla's $70 million AI jackpot comes from over a million AI domain registrations, with the island's .ai domain code being assigned back in the '90s.
- Siri's Gemini upgrade is expected to launch in February, allowing it to handle tasks more efficiently and making it a competitor to other chatbots like ChatGPT.
- Google's GIST method guarantees that its selections hit at least 50% of optimal value, providing a "safety net" for ML teams when training on billions of data points.
- Rokid's AI Glasses have a 12MP camera, capture 4K photos and 3K video, and support real-time translation in 12 languages.
- Other AI tools mentioned include Notis, Remio, MessageMosaic, CoreWise, BidHelm, ReadDocs, Linkdify, and TalkWiz.
- The newsletter also mentions a paradox bridge builder prompt, which helps users map inner conflicts and turn them into small, low-risk experiments.
- There's An AI For That gear is available, including hoodies, hats, tees, sweatshirts, and mugs.
- The newsletter provides information on how to update email preferences and unsubscribe.

### Key Highlights
- Deel is under a criminal investigation by the DOJ for allegedly recruiting a spy within rival firm Rippling.

- OpenEvidence has hit a $12B valuation after a $250M Series D funding round.

- Deel is facing a criminal investigation by the DOJ for allegedly recruiting a spy within Rippling, with grand-jury subpoenas issued to collect information.
- OpenAI and Cerebras have partnered to use Cerebras chips for Codex inference and a new voice mode, known as "Garlic."
- OpenEvidence has reached a $12B valuation after a $250M Series D funding round, co-led by Thrive Capital and DST Global.
- Wikipedia has entered paid agreements with major AI companies like Meta, Microsoft, and Perplexity for structured data access.
- Moonshot AI has been valued at $4.8B following a recent funding round, up from $4.3B, with backing from Alibaba.

- Zipline has secured a $600M funding round at a $7.6B valuation, with investment from Fidelity and Baillie Gifford.

## TLDR Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Apple's AI efforts have resulted in a Google partnership, management changes, and two new versions of Siri, with an announcement planned for the second half of February.
- ChatGPT's lead in AI traffic has shrunk as Gemini surges, marking a significant acceleration of competitive pressure.
- Nebius Token Factory offers production inference for open-source LLMs, delivering managed inference with explicit control over execution paths.
- Blue Origin has made impressive strides with reuse, with the next launch of its New Glenn rocket set to refly a booster.
- A new experimental drug using CRISPR has been shown to cut harmful cholesterol levels in half with one-time gene editing.

### Detailed Points
- **Apple's AI Efforts**: Apple has partnered with Google, made management changes, and is planning to release two new versions of Siri. The company had considered partnering with OpenAI or Anthropic but ultimately chose Google due to its improved technology and reasonable financial structure.
- **ChatGPT and Gemini**: ChatGPT's worldwide traffic declined in January, while Google's Gemini saw an increase in traffic, reflecting Google's systematic integration across its services and devices.
- **Nebius Token Factory**: Nebius Token Factory is built for teams running open-source LLMs in real products, offering managed inference with speculative decoding, cache-aware routing, and post-training tuned to real traffic.
- **Blue Origin**: Blue Origin's next launch will refly a booster from its second mission, with a turnaround time of less than four months, which is impressive even for a well-capitalized program.
- **Gene Editing Drug**: A new experimental drug using CRISPR has been shown to cut harmful cholesterol levels in half with one-time gene editing, although its long-term safety is unknown.
- **Tesla and Autopilot**: Tesla will start charging $99 per month for its Full Self-Driving (FSD) subscription, with the capability available for a one-time fee of $8,000 until February 14.
- **Vimeo's Slow Fade**: Vimeo, which started before YouTube in 2004, was acquired by Bending Spoons in September last year, marking a decline in its fortunes.
- **Google's Sideload Warning**: Google is introducing a "high-friction" sideloading flow to Android, which will add extra steps when installing apps from unverified developers.
- **Job Opportunities**: TLDR is hiring a Senior Software Engineer, Applied AI, with a salary range of $200k-$300k, and is also looking for referrals.

## Staying Ahead with AI

### Key Highlights
- The newsletter discusses the setup of a 24/7 AI assistant, specifically highlighting Clawdbot, a self-hosted AI agent.
- Clawdbot has gained significant attention on Tech Twitter, with over 18,000 GitHub stars in three weeks.
- The assistant can be deployed on Telegram in 5 minutes and offers features like persistent memory, proactive messaging, and full computer access.

### Detailed Points
- Clawdbot is a personal AI agent that can be integrated with messaging apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, or Discord, providing a unique way to interact with AI.
- The AI agent has three key capabilities: persistent memory across conversations, proactive messaging (it can initiate conversations), and full computer access for tasks like terminal commands and browser automation.
- Clawdbot uses the Anthropic API for its AI capabilities, and setting it up involves model authentication, channel connections, and workspace setup.
- There are two paths for setting up Clawdbot: testing locally, which is good for experimentation but has limitations like the assistant sleeping when the laptop sleeps, and a production setup on a Hetzner VPS for 24/7 availability at a low cost (~$5/month).
- The production setup involves using a VPS, setting up Tailscale for secure remote access, and connecting the messaging channel (e.g., Telegram).
- Important considerations include security hardening, such as enabling pairing for unknown senders, keeping the Gateway on loopback, setting API spending limits, and enabling sandboxing for group chats.
- Common errors and troubleshooting steps are discussed, including running `clawdbot doctor` to identify misconfigurations and `clawdbot status --all` for a detailed debug report.
- Other tools mentioned include Blinky, an open-source AI debugging agent for VSCode; CodeSquire, an AI code assistant for data scientists; and Code to Flow, a tool that converts code into interactive flowcharts or diagrams.
- The newsletter also mentions The Marketing Millennials, a free newsletter that provides marketing ideas and insights.

newsletters.summary:
## JournalClub.io

### Key Highlights
- Researchers from Dalian University of Technology in China have presented a novel image-fusion method for a special type of CMOS sensor that captures three different responses in a single exposure: high-gain linear, low-gain linear, and logarithmic.
- The method combines dual conversion gain (DCG) and logarithmic response pixels to extend the dynamic range of the sensor, reducing motion artifacts and ghosting.
- The algorithm assigns weights to each pixel across the images based on quality measures such as edge strength, local intensity variation, and exposure-related weighting.

### Detailed Points
- The traditional solution to limited dynamic range is multi-exposure HDR, which captures the same scene multiple times with different exposure settings and merges the images together. However, this approach has a flaw: motion artifacts.
- Single-exposure HDR methods, such as DCG and lateral overflow integration capacitor (LOFIC), try to capture a wide dynamic range in one shot, avoiding motion artifacts.
- Logarithmic response pixels compress the signal, representing a huge range of brightness levels with a limited range of digital values. However, they often fall apart in low light due to noise.
- The authors' proposed setup combines DCG and logarithmic response with a charge compensation mechanism, allowing the sensor to capture three different responses in a single exposure.
- The pixel contains a pinned photodiode, a transfer gate, a floating diffusion node, and a source follower, and has three readout steps in one exposure: high-gain, low-gain, and logarithmic.
- The fusion stage operates at the pixel level, asking which measurement is likely to be the most reliable representation of the scene radiance, and computes multiple quality measures independently on each response image.
- The algorithm multiplies the quality measures instead of summing them, making the fusion mechanism conservative and down-weighting pixels that are sharp but saturated, or well-exposed but noisy.
- The resulting per-pixel weights are normalized across the three response images, and the fusion is performed in the frequency domain using a multiscale pyramid.
- The authors tested their system by capturing real-world scenes with a ton of lighting variation and examined the images individually and after fusion, demonstrating that their method produces images that preserve detail across the entire scene with smoother transitions and fewer artifacts.

## TLDR AI

### Key Highlights
- Apple plans to unveil a Gemini-powered Siri assistant in February, leveraging Google's AI models to enhance task completion using user data.
- OpenAI is adding a dedicated shopping cart section to ChatGPT and support for personal responses in temporary chat sessions.
- Modulate introduces Ensemble Listening Models (ELMs), a new AI architecture that orchestrates 100+ voice-specific models for better conversation understanding.
- SerpApi offers a web search API for AI, allowing companies like Perplexity, NVIDIA, and Ahrefs to scrape search results.

### Detailed Points
- Apple's Gemini-powered Siri assistant will have an even more advanced version with conversational capabilities akin to ChatGPT, to be revealed at the Worldwide Developers Conference in June.
- OpenAI's shopping cart feature will serve as a centralized space for reviewing selected items and finalizing purchases, while personal responses will balance privacy with customized assistance.
- Modulate's ELM, Velma, is now publicly available, offering benefits such as decoding intent, emotion, stress, and authenticity in messy, multilingual audio, and being 100x faster, cheaper, and more accurate than LLMs.
- SerpApi provides a fast, easy, and complete way to scrape search results, with a 50% discount available for new customers on their first 3 months.
- Other notable developments include the introduction of Claude Chic, an alternative to Claude Code, and Video Arena's expansion from Discord to a public web interface.
- Research papers and projects discussed include "Challenges and Research Directions for Large Language Model Inference Hardware," "Reinforcement Learning at Test Time," and "Diffusion-Based Code Modeling."
- The newsletter also covers various job openings and opportunities at TLDR, including applications and referrals.
